description: Batching sweep workloads (Phase 0 of the batching investigation; ai-dotnet/benchmarks/README.md, 'Batching sweep'). Built at load from text already in the repository, deterministically (System.Random with 'seed'): no file outside Git, no download. Embedding models (e5, EmbeddingGemma 2 text) draw from the MIRACL retrieval set: 'short' are real search queries (8 languages), 'medium' single Wikipedia passages, 'long' a passage and the passages after it in corpus order, same language, joined with a space while the joined text stays within 'long_tokens' model tokens (prompt or prefix included), starting from passages in seeded order; a joined text below 'long_min_fraction' of the target is dropped. GLiNER2 draws from the WNUT-17 test sentences (social media text, one label set for every item, as one GLiNER2 call requires): 'short' one sentence, 'medium' 2 to 4 consecutive sentences, 'long' consecutive sentences up to 'long_tokens' (schema prefix included). 'mixed' draws each item's category with the 'mixed' probabilities (a retrieval or extraction service sees mostly short and medium inputs with a long tail), then the next unused item of that category in shuffled order. Every item longer than the model's per-sequence limit is dropped. Pools are the first 'pool' items of each category after a seeded shuffle (only those are tokenized); a call of batch b takes b consecutive pool items starting at call_index x b (wrapping), whichever worker runs it. Quality: every item's output in every timed call is compared with the same item run alone at load (profile tolerance padded_batch_vs_single_*).
